page_title: Building Hacker News with Angular 2 CLI, RxJS and Webpack

summary.title: Building Hacker News with Angular 2 CLI, RxJS and Webpack
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a Hacker News client in Angular 2 using Angular CLI, RxJS Observables for async data, and the Angular component router, then how to cut request overhead by switching to an unofficial single-request API.
takeaways: Angular CLI scaffolds components and modules, and the project now bundles with Webpack instead of SystemJS.
The @NgModule decorator declares components, imports and providers, and a service listed in providers gives a single shared instance.

Observables from RxJS are subscribed to for async data; the author uses one request per item and then finds that too slow, switching to an unofficial API that returns an item with its details in one request.
Angular Component Router routes map paths to StoriesComponent and ItemCommentsComponent, passing story type and page or id through route data and params.
View encapsulation (None, Emulated, Native) explains why global body styles fail in a child component and how to fix them with ViewEncapsulation.None.
summary.summary: The author walks through building a Hacker News front page, comments and user profile views in Angular 2 with Angular CLI. The post covers components, Sass styling, view encapsulation, the NgModule decorator, and Observable-based data services built on the official Hacker News API. It then shows the performance problem of one request per item and replaces it with an unofficial API that returns full item details in one call. The tutorial finishes with routing, comment trees and a production build command.
